records.title: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS Command Injection Vulnerability
records.description: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect feature contains a command injection vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute commands with root privileges on the firewall.
records.action: Apply mitigations per vendor instructions as they become available. Otherwise, users with vulnerable versions of affected devices should enable Threat Prevention IDs available from the vendor. See the vendor bulletin for more details and a patch release schedule.
affected: PAN-OS: 10.2.0 to < 10.2.9-h1 (status changes within range; see CNA record)
PAN-OS: 11.0.0 to < 11.0.4-h1 (status changes within range; see CNA record)
PAN-OS: 11.1.0 to < 11.1.2-h3 (status changes within range; see CNA record)
conditions:
This issue is applicable only to PAN-OS 10.2, PAN-OS 11.0, and PAN-OS 11.1 firewalls configured with GlobalProtect gateway or GlobalProtect portal (or both). Device telemetry does not need to be enabled for PAN-OS firewalls to be exposed to attacks related to this vulnerability.

You can verify whether you have a GlobalProtect gateway or GlobalProtect portal configured by checking for entries in your firewall web interface (Network > GlobalProtect > Gateways or Network > GlobalProtect > Portals).

records.title: Compromised CA keys and root removal
records.description: Weak intermediate CA keys permit forged certificates against unprotected clients. Root removal can also break legitimate certificate chains.
records.action: Update OS and application trust bundles, including containers and bundled runtimes. Replace affected server certificates through a trusted alternate hierarchy and test client connections.
steps: Find affected server chains and all client trust stores, including Java, Node.js and containers.
Apply each platform vendor’s trust-store update and redeploy long-running processes.
Replace affected server chains and verify representative browser and application clients.
Record deployed package/build versions and connection test results.

conditions:

Access to the public portion of the VeloCloud Edge authentication certificate is required. A successful attack requires network access to the VCO web interface. Deployments that restrict VCO web interface access to trusted administrative networks can reduce risk of exposure.
